candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because the downstream order service returns HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders; the gateway's own handling is fast and healthy.
candidates.uncertainty: Order-side root cause (db pool, redis, payment) not observable from gateway evidence; order service telemetry required to localize further.

report.explanation: Traces and logs show gateway POST /v1/checkout failing with 502 in 16-63ms, each paired with a client call to order:8000/v1/orders returning 500. Gateway /readyz and /healthz are 200 and fast, so the gateway itself is healthy; the failure originates in the order service. Current evidence bounds the fault to the order dependency but does not establish which internal cause, so only the http-500 candidate is supported.
missing_evidence: Order service traces/logs for POST /v1/orders to identify the internal 500 cause
Order service dependency metrics (postgresql pool, redis, payment) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion, redis-timeout, downstream-latency
